Tokenize and Analyze Multiple Texts with Explicit Document IDs

lexdiv_text_batch.Rd

Read named texts, data frames, or tibbles into complete tokenizations, then compute lexical diversity (including multi-parameter plan profiles) while retaining document-local audits and preprocessing provenance.

Usage

lexdiv_tokenize_batch(
  documents,
  id_col = "document_id",
  text_col = "text",
  normalization = "NFC",
  case = "lower",
  keep_numbers = FALSE,
  tokenizer = "english"
)

lexdiv_metrics_text_batch(
  documents,
  id_col = "document_id",
  text_col = "text",
  unit = "surface",
  word_inclusion = "all",
  normalization = "NFC",
  case = "lower",
  keep_numbers = FALSE,
  tokenizer = "english",
  ...,
  plan = NULL,
  max_rows = 1e6,
  metadata = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_text_batch_results'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_text_batch_results'
plot(x, ..., monochrome = FALSE)

Arguments

documents

A named character vector, a data frame/tibble with ID and text columns, or (for lexdiv_metrics_text_batch()) a named list of lexdiv_tokenization objects.

id_col, text_col

Names of the selected ID and text columns.

unit, word_inclusion

Lexical-unit and word-inclusion settings.

normalization, case, keep_numbers, tokenizer

Preprocessing settings for raw text inputs (defaulting to normalization = "NFC", case = "lower", keep_numbers = FALSE, tokenizer = "english").

...

For lexdiv_metrics_text_batch(), metric arguments forwarded to lexdiv_metrics_text when plan is NULL. For print() and plot(), arguments passed to the underlying method.

plan

Optional normalized request plan from lexdiv_plan.

max_rows

Row ceiling when plan is supplied.

metadata

Optional document metadata data frame/tibble matched by document_id.

x

A lexdiv_text_batch_results object.

monochrome

Logical switch for black/grey plotting.

Value

lexdiv_tokenize_batch() returns an input-ordered named list of lexdiv_tokenization objects. lexdiv_metrics_text_batch() returns a lexdiv_text_batch_results list with results, token_audit, preprocessing, and optional metadata, which pipes directly into lexdiv_widen, lexdiv_screen_lengths, and lexdiv_study_table.

See also

lexdiv_metrics_text, lexdiv_study_table, lexdiv_widen

Examples

texts <- data.frame(
  document_id = c("essay_a", "essay_b", "empty"),
  text = c("Cats chase cats and dogs.", "The reader reads a story.", "")
)
result <- lexdiv_metrics_text_batch(texts, metrics = "ttr")
lexdiv_widen(result)
#> <lexdiv_wide_results: 3 rows; 12 columns>
#>   document_id ttr__value ttr__status ttr__missing_reason  ttr__method_id
#> 1     essay_a        0.8          ok                <NA> ttr_v_over_n_v1
#> 2     essay_b        1.0          ok                <NA> ttr_v_over_n_v1
#> 3       empty         NA     missing         empty_input ttr_v_over_n_v1
#>   ttr__below_quality_floor       ttr__metric_contract_id
#> 1                    FALSE ldfreq-lexical-diversity-core
#> 2                    FALSE ldfreq-lexical-diversity-core
#> 3                     TRUE ldfreq-lexical-diversity-core
#>   ttr__metric_contract_version ttr__requested_parameters
#> 1                        0.2.0                          
#> 2                        0.2.0                          
#> 3                        0.2.0                          
#>   ttr__effective_parameters ttr__N ttr__V
#> 1                                5      4
#> 2                                5      5
#> 3                                0      0
plot(result, metric_id = "ttr")


# Direct plan execution on raw texts:
plan <- lexdiv_plan(presets = character(), specs = list(
  lexdiv_spec("ttr", request_id = "ttr")
))
planned <- lexdiv_metrics_text_batch(texts, plan = plan)
planned$results[, c("document_id", "request_id", "value", "status")]
#> <lexdiv_profile_batch_results: 3 documents; 3 specification results; schema unknown>
#>   document_id request_id value  status
#> 1     essay_a        ttr   0.8      ok
#> 2     essay_b        ttr   1.0      ok
#> 3       empty        ttr    NA missing
